title: Constants, closed-form microstrip and stripline models, differential fits and lines of a stack-up

cases.title: Speed of light in vacuum
cases.tolerance_note: exact by definition of the metre, so no difference is accepted
cases.source: The International System of Units (SI Brochure), the definition of the metre: c = 299 792 458 m/s

cases.title: Permeability of vacuum
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the recommended value has twelve significant digits and the code stores the same twelve
cases.source: CODATA recommended values (2018 adjustment): mu0 = 1.256 637 062 12(19) e-6 N/A^2

cases.title: Impedance of free space
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the code computes mu0 times c, which agrees with the recommended value to better than one part in 1e11
cases.source: CODATA recommended values (2018 adjustment): Z0 = 376.730 313 668(57) ohm

cases.title: Complete elliptic integral K at k = 1/sqrt(2)
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the arithmetic-geometric mean converges to rounding error, and k itself is rounded to a double
cases.source: Abramowitz and Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, section 17.3 (K at m = 1/2 is Gamma(1/4)^2 / (4 sqrt(pi)) = 1.854 074 677 301 372)

cases.title: Zero-thickness stripline in air at k = 1/sqrt(2): Z0 = eta0/4
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the width ratio 2 asinh(1)/pi is the one that makes k = sech(pi W / 2b) equal 1/sqrt(2), where K(k) = K'(k) and Z0 = eta0/4 exactly
cases.source: S. B. Cohn, Characteristic impedance of the shielded-strip transmission line (IRE Trans. MTT, 1954): Z0 = (eta0 / (4 sqrt(er))) K(k)/K'(k), with eta0/4 from CODATA Z0 = 376.730 313 668 ohm

cases.title: Same stripline in a dielectric of relative permittivity 4: Z0 = eta0/(4 sqrt(er))
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the same identity divided by the square root of the permittivity
cases.source: S. B. Cohn, Characteristic impedance of the shielded-strip transmission line (IRE Trans. MTT, 1954), with eta0 from CODATA

cases.title: Closed-form stripline of zero thickness against the exact value at k = 1/sqrt(2)
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the closed form is documented as within about one per cent of the exact zero-thickness value
cases.source: S. B. Cohn, Characteristic impedance of the shielded-strip transmission line (IRE Trans. MTT, 1954): the exact value Z0 = eta0/4 at this width

cases.title: Microstrip in air has an effective permittivity of exactly 1
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: a value that follows from the definition (no dielectric), so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: Definition of the effective permittivity of a line: the ratio of the capacitance with the dielectric to the capacitance with air; with er = 1 it is 1 (Hammerstad and Jensen, 1980, eps_eff -> 1 as er -> 1)

cases.title: 50 ohm microstrip of the worked example: W/d = 3.081 on er = 2.2
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the book gives the width from the Wheeler and Schneider formulas and the code uses Hammerstad and Jensen; one per cent is wider than the known difference between them
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, microstrip chapter, worked example of a 50 ohm line on er = 2.2, d = 0.127 cm: W/d = 3.081 (W = 3.91287 mm here)

cases.title: Effective permittivity of the same microstrip
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the book rounds to three digits and uses a simpler formula than the code
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, microstrip chapter, the same worked example: eps_e = 1.87

cases.title: Microstrip against the closed form of IPC-2141 (W 0.35 mm, T 35 um, H 0.2 mm, er 4.5)
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the closed form of IPC-2141 is an approximation that differs from Hammerstad and Jensen by a few per cent in its range; six per cent is wider than that gap, so the case only catches a wrong formula
cases.source: IPC-2141 (Controlled Impedance Circuit Boards and High Speed Logic Design), microstrip: Z0 = 87/sqrt(er + 1.41) ln(5.98 H / (0.8 W + T)), valid for 0.1 < W/H < 2.0 and 1 < er < 15, evaluated for these inputs

cases.title: Microstrip against the closed form of IPC-2141 (W 0.3 mm, T 35 um, H 0.2 mm, er 4.2)
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: as for the other case of this formula, wider than the known gap between the two approximations
cases.source: IPC-2141, microstrip: Z0 = 87/sqrt(er + 1.41) ln(5.98 H / (0.8 W + T)), evaluated for these inputs

cases.title: Stripline against the closed form of IPC-2141 (W 0.15 mm, T 35 um, b 1.0 mm, er 4.5)
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: both forms are narrow-strip approximations that agree within a per cent or two in the range of the formula
cases.source: IPC-2141, stripline: Z0 = 60/sqrt(er) ln(4 b / (0.67 pi (0.8 W + T))), valid for W/b < 0.35 and T/b < 0.25, evaluated for these inputs

cases.title: Stripline against the closed form of IPC-2141 (W 0.2 mm, T 17.5 um, b 0.9 mm, er 4.2)
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: as for the other case of this formula
cases.source: IPC-2141, stripline: Z0 = 60/sqrt(er) ln(4 b / (0.67 pi (0.8 W + T))), valid for W/b < 0.35 and T/b < 0.25, evaluated for these inputs

cases.title: Differential microstrip fit of IPC-2141 for Z0 = 50 ohm and S = H
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the fit is a closed formula, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: IPC-2141, edge-coupled microstrip pair: Zdiff = 2 Z0 (1 - 0.48 exp(-0.96 S/H)), evaluated for these inputs

cases.title: Differential stripline fit of IPC-2141 for Z0 = 50 ohm and S = b
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the fit is a closed formula, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: IPC-2141, edge-coupled stripline pair: Zdiff = 2 Z0 (1 - 0.347 exp(-2.9 S/b)), evaluated for these inputs

cases.title: Skin depth of copper at 1 GHz
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the formula is exact for the conductivity used; the code reads the conductivity of the settings, 5.8e7 S/m, and the reference uses the same value
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the skin effect: delta = sqrt(2 / (omega mu sigma)) = 1 / sqrt(pi f mu0 sigma), for sigma = 5.8e7 S/m (annealed copper, 100 % IACS) at 1 GHz

cases.title: Delay of a stripline in a homogeneous dielectric of relative permittivity 4
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: in a homogeneous dielectric the wave travels at c/sqrt(er) exactly, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, TEM lines: the phase velocity is c/sqrt(er), so the delay is sqrt(er)/c = 2/299 792 458 s/m = 6.6713 ps/mm

cases.title: Effective permittivity of a stripline in a homogeneous dielectric
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: all the field is in one dielectric, so the effective permittivity is the relative permittivity
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, TEM lines: with the field wholly in a dielectric of relative permittivity er, the effective permittivity is er
